For a non-dormant Class 12 insurer the SCR is the one-year value-at-risk of basic own-funds at a 90 percent confidence level. min_capital.Class 12 dormant insurer: The minimum capital requirement equals the solvency capital requirement. For a dormant insurer that requirement is the regulatory capital needed so that assets exceed liabilities, including operational-management and regulatory-compliance liabilities
min_capital.Class 12 long-term business: Long-term Class 12 contracts, within classes 1, 2 and 10, are covered by the Insurance (Long-Term Business Valuation and Solvency) Regulations 2021 rather than the non-life floor above. A separate sterling floor for that long-term business was not located in the materials reviewed
min_capital.Class 13 insurance special purpose vehic: Must be fully funded at all times, with total adjusted net assets covering maximum aggregate exposure (Insurance Regulations 2025, Schedule 2). Class 13 is supplemental and does not by itself authorise insurance business. No separate fixed sterling floor was extracted

A 20 percent rate applies to income from Isle of Man land and property and, from 6 April 2024, to petroleum extraction. Insurance is not one of those categories. No premium-tax rate is set in the Authority's Fees Order. The regulatory charge is the annual fee.

name: Jersey

The JFSC maintains the discretion to amend capital requirements based on business projections.

name: Kansas

Association captives can utilize letters of credit from state-chartered banks for capital requirements. The domicile leverages the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority for admission documents.
tax_notes: Tax paid on all premiums received on risks in the state

name: Kazakhstan
summary: The Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) is a unique hub that offers incentives to attract Kazakhstani capital and assets back from foreign jurisdictions. It provides three captive classes and utilizes a specific formula to calculate the premium risk component of capital. The jurisdiction is noted for its relocation-friendly regime, exemplified by the move of the Kazakhstan Energy Reinsurance Company from Bermuda.
legislation: AIFC Insurance and Reinsurance Prudential Rules
tax_notes: Friendly tax regime and operational incentives

name: Kentucky
summary: Kentucky is an established midwestern domicile that has grown to over 80 licensed captives across diverse industries like healthcare, banking, and manufacturing. It features a dedicated staff and graduated premium tax rates that become lower as premium volumes rise. A minimum annual tax of $5,000 is required if regular premium taxes fall below that threshold.
tax_notes: $5,000 minimum annual premium tax

name: Labuan
summary: Labuan IBFC is Asia's premier international financial hub, uniquely offering shariah-compliant Islamic captives, known as takaful captives. It is a substance-enabling jurisdiction with access to Malaysia's network of over 70 double taxation treaties. Every captive must have an operational office in Labuan or appoint a licensed underwriting manager.
legislation: Labuan Islamic Financial Services and Securities Act 2010

min_capital.Requirement: Risk-commensurate working funds in a Labuan bank

tax_notes: Fiscal neutrality and certainty

name: Liechtenstein
summary: Liechtenstein offers an adept workforce and unique central European access to both the EU and Switzerland markets. Captives are subject to Solvency II and can insure subsidiaries across the European Economic Area and third countries. While it does not tax capital, it applies a flat 12.5% tax rate on taxable income.
tax_notes: 12.5% flat tax on income; CHF 30,000 license fee

name: Luxembourg
summary: Luxembourg authorises captive insurance undertakings and captive reinsurance undertakings under the Law of 7 December 2015 on the insurance sector, as amended, and the Commissariat aux Assurances supervises them. The Law of 21 July 2021 moved the grant and withdrawal of authorisation from the Minister to the CAA. A reinsurance undertaking must be effectively run by at least one natural-person reinsurance executive, or by a CAA-authorised reinsurance management company represented by such an executive. In CAA Regulation 15/03, consolidated at 27 January 2023, the absolute floor of the minimum capital requirement is EUR 1,300,000 for a captive reinsurer and EUR 3,900,000 for any other reinsurer. Captive insurers use the ordinary insurance floors: EUR 2,700,000 for non-life, EUR 4,000,000 where liability classes 10 to 15 are covered, and EUR 4,000,000 for life. At 1 July 2026 the CAA reported 207 Luxembourg-law reinsurance undertakings and a total staff of 93. It does not publish a captive-only census or a captive-unit headcount. It described 12 new reinsurance authorisations in 2025 and 3 in the first half of 2026 as confirming renewed interest in reinsurance captives. Corporate income tax, in the income-tax law in force at 1 January 2026, is 14 percent up to EUR 175,000 of taxable income and 16 percent above EUR 200,000.
legislation: Law of 7 December 2015 on the insurance sector, as amended (consolidated text as of 3 April 2026), and Commissariat aux Assurances Regulation No. 15/03 of 7 December 2015, as amended
applicable_legislation: Law of 7 December 2015 on the insurance sector, as amended, including the definitions of captive insurance undertaking and captive reinsurance undertaking and Article 112 on the minimum capital requirement (CAA English consolidation as of 3 April 2026); Law of 21 July 2021, which transferred authorisation from the Minister to the CAA; CAA Regulation No. 15/03 of 7 December 2015 on insurance and reinsurance undertakings, as amended (English consolidation as of 27 January 2023, Article 52); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 5 December 2007 on the authorisation and exercise of reinsurance undertakings, as amended, on the provision pour fluctuation de sinistralité; CAA Circular 22/10 on annual reinsurance reporting; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 April 2014, as amended by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 December 2020, on contributions to CAA staff and operating costs; amended Law of 4 December 1967 on income tax, Articles 167 and 174 (coordinated text in force at 1 January 2026).

min_capital.Captive reinsurance undertaking: Absolute floor of the minimum capital requirement EUR 1,300,000 (CAA Regulation 15/03, Article 52(2)(c), consolidation of 27 January 2023)
min_capital.Non-life insurance, including a captive: Absolute floor EUR 2,700,000, or EUR 4,000,000 where any risk in classes 10 to 15 of Annex I, Part A, of the 2015 law is covered (Article 52(2)(a))
min_capital.MCR relative to the SCR: The minimum capital requirement must not fall below 25 percent, and must not exceed 45 percent, of the solvency capital requirement including any capital add-on (Article 52(3)). It is calculated at least quarterly

tax_notes: Captive insurers and reinsurers are taxed as companies. Article 174 of the amended Law of 4 December 1967, in the Administration des contributions directes coordinated text in force at 1 January 2026, sets corporate income tax at 14 percent where taxable income does not exceed EUR 175,000, at EUR 24,500 plus 30 percent of the income above EUR 175,000 where taxable income is between EUR 175,000 and EUR 200,001, and at 16 percent above EUR 200,000. Guichet.lu, updated 7 April 2026, states that a further 7 percent of the corporate income tax is charged for the employment fund. The rate table on that Guichet page still describes the 2019 schedule of 15 and 17 percent and was not used for the rates above. Article 167 allows deduction of technical-provision allocations by insurance and reinsurance undertakings to the extent they correspond to obligations owed to insureds at the year-end, on conditions set by grand-ducal regulation. Every reinsurance undertaking must also constitute a provision pour fluctuation de sinistralité under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 5 December 2007, as amended. The texts reviewed do not state, as a captive-specific rule, that this fluctuation provision is deductible in full. Municipal business tax and net wealth tax also apply; commune rates and the net-wealth tariff were not verified here. No premium-tax rate was found in the 2015 insurance-sector law materials reviewed.
contact_name: Commissariat aux Assurances

fees.licensing_incorporation: No fixed captive application fee is stated on the CAA laws or regulations pages reviewed. The CAA annual report for 2025-2026 says staff and operating costs, other than retired-staff pensions, are met by taxes paid by supervised undertakings and by a state grant. Those taxes are set by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 April 2014, as amended by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 December 2020. The euro schedule in that regulation was not extracted in this verification.
fees.annual_fees: Annual contributions to CAA staff and operating costs are set by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 April 2014, as amended on 19 December 2020. A current euro amount for a captive or reinsurance undertaking was not extracted from that regulation.
fees.premium_tax_rate: No premium-tax rate is set in the Law of 7 December 2015 materials reviewed. Corporate income tax applies under Article 174 of the income-tax law, at 14 percent up to EUR 175,000 of taxable income and 16 percent above EUR 200,000, plus the 7 percent employment-fund charge stated by Guichet.lu.

annual_filing_requirements: Insurance and reinsurance undertakings calculate the minimum capital requirement at least quarterly and report it to the CAA (Regulation 15/03, Article 52(4)). Reinsurance undertakings file an annual report. Circular 22/10 requires the claims-fluctuation-provision ceiling table, and the components of the annual movement where the provision exceeds 30 percent of the theoretical maximum. The 2025-2026 annual report says Circular 24/3, as modified by Circulars 25/5 and 25/6, splits the statutory auditor's separate report for reinsurance undertakings into a distinct report and a complementary distinct report, with different submission dates. Those day-counts were not extracted from the circulars. A change in ownership of a captive insurer or a reinsurance undertaking is notified on the forms introduced by Circular 24/9.

name: Malta
summary: Malta is the only EU member state with protected cell company (PCC) legislation that extends to brokers and insurance managers beyond traditional insurers. Its PCCs offer unique shared economies of scale and direct access to the EU market, effectively reducing fronting costs. The domicile is Fitch A+ rated and focuses on facilitating blockchain technology and legal certainty for smart contracts.
tax_notes: Direct access to UK and EU markets

name: Mauritius
summary: Mauritius is an emerging African domicile that provides stability with no exchange controls and an innovative pool of financial products. New proposed rules distinguish four classes of captive business based on the percentage of gross written premium originating from affiliates. Minimum unimpaired paid-up capital starts at approximately $86,750 for pure captives.
tax_notes: Long-standing bilateral relations with Africa

name: Michigan
summary: Michigan licenses a wide range of captives, including non-profit pure and special purpose financial captives. It maintains a strict resident requirement where two out of three organizers must be state residents, and board meetings must be held in-state. Notably, the state does not have a premium tax rate, using a renewal fee based on premium volume instead.
tax_notes: No tax rate; premium-volume based renewal fee

name: Missouri
summary: Missouri licenses captive insurers under sections 379.1300 to 379.1351, RSMo, enacted in 2007, and special purpose life reinsurance captives under sections 379.1353 to 379.1421, administered by the Department of Commerce and Insurance. The Department's February 2026 fact sheet states that 55 captives were active as of 1 February 2026 and that Missouri captives reported $8.6 billion of gross written premium in 2025. It does not publish a type split, a formation count, or a surrender count. A pure captive holds at least $250,000. An association, industrial insured, or sponsored captive holds at least $500,000. A special purpose life reinsurance captive maintains at least $250,000 of surplus in cash in Missouri. A branch captive posts a United States trust of not less than the pure-captive minimum plus the reserves on branch business. The license fee is $7,500 and the annual renewal fee is $7,500, and both are deductible from premium tax. A special purpose life reinsurance captive also pays a $10,000 application fee under 20 CSR 200-20.030. The Department's 2026 handout states that application and license amount as $17,500. Direct premium tax is 0.380 percent, 0.285 percent, 0.190 percent, and 0.072 percent on successive $20 million bands. Assumed-reinsurance tax is 0.214 percent, 0.143 percent, 0.048 percent, and 0.024 percent. The minimum is $7,500 and the maximum is $200,000. The return is due 1 February and the tax is due 1 May. Sam Komo is Captive Program Manager. The published filings address is INCaptiveFilings@insurance.mo.gov. No licensing-time standard and no staff count are published.
legislation: Revised Statutes of Missouri sections 379.1300 to 379.1351 (Captive Insurance Companies) and sections 379.1353 to 379.1421 (Special Purpose Life Reinsurance Captives), and 20 CSR 200-20
applicable_legislation: Sections 379.1300 to 379.1351, RSMo, originating in 2007 Senate Bill 215. Capital and surplus are section 379.1306, amended in 2013. The license, in-state requirements, and fees are section 379.1302, amended in 2009. Reports are section 379.1312, amended in 2013. Examinations are section 379.1314. Premium tax is section 379.1326, amended in 2013. Branch security is section 379.1342. Special purpose life reinsurance captives are sections 379.1353 to 379.1421, originating in 2007 Senate Bill 215. Minimum surplus and the license are section 379.1359. The SPLRC license fee is section 379.1364. The SPLRC audit is section 379.1403. SPLRC premium tax is section 379.1412, amended in 2009. Admission fees and the annual audit are also in 20 CSR 200-20.

min_capital.Pure captive: Not less than $250,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus (section 379.1306.1(1)). The Department's 2026 types sheet states the same figure.
min_capital.Sponsored captive: Not less than $500,000 (section 379.1306.1(4)). The Department's types sheet states that the core's minimum is $500,000 and does not state a separate dollar floor for a cell.
min_capital.Branch captive: Section 379.1342 requires a United States trust, funded by an irrevocable letter of credit or other acceptable asset, of not less than the pure-captive minimum in section 379.1306.1(1) plus the reserves on branch policies and reinsurance contracts, including loss reserves, allocated loss-adjustment expenses, incurred-but-not-reported losses, and unearned premiums. The director may allow a reduction for security already posted with a reinsurer. The Department's types sheet states a $250,000 minimum placed in trust, an irrevocable letter of credit, or other acceptable assets for the benefit of U.S. policyholders.
min_capital.Special purpose life reinsurance captive: A minimum surplus in Missouri, in cash, of $250,000 (section 379.1359(5)). The Department's types sheet states the same $250,000 minimum capitalization.
min_capital.Form of capital: For a captive under sections 379.1300 to 379.1351, cash or an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a Missouri-chartered bank or a Federal Reserve member bank and approved by the director. The director may prescribe additional capital based on the type, volume, and nature of the business. An SPLRC's minimum surplus is cash held in Missouri.

tax_notes: Section 379.1326 taxes direct premiums, after return premiums and policyholder dividends or premium deposits returned or credited, at 0.380 percent on the first $20 million, 0.285 percent on the next $20 million, 0.190 percent on the next $20 million, and 0.072 percent thereafter. Annuity considerations are not taxed. Assumed-reinsurance premiums are taxed at 0.214 percent, 0.143 percent, 0.048 percent, and 0.024 percent on those same bands. Reinsurance tax does not apply to risks taxed on a direct basis, or to a qualifying assumption of loss reserves and other liabilities of another insurer under common ownership and control that is part of a plan to discontinue that insurer. The annual minimum aggregate tax is $7,500 and the annual maximum is $200,000. For a sponsored captive the $7,500 minimum applies to the company as a whole and not to each protected cell, and the cells are not subject to the minimum. The maximum for a protected cell is calculated under the direct-premium subsection, and the sponsored captive remits the aggregate of the cells' tax liabilities. Captives under common ownership and control are taxed as one captive. Common ownership and control is 80 percent of the voting stock, of the surplus and voting power of a mutual or nonprofit, or of the membership interest of a limited liability company. The tax is in lieu of other occupation taxes, except ad valorem taxes on real and personal property used to produce income. The return is due 1 February. The director certifies the tax by 31 March, and payment to the director of revenue is due 1 May. The license fee and the renewal fee may be deducted from the premium tax. An SPLRC is taxed under section 379.1412 on assumed reinsurance at the same 0.214 percent, 0.143 percent, 0.048 percent, and 0.024 percent bands, with the same $7,500 minimum and $200,000 maximum, and may also deduct its application, license, and renewal fees. A fee deduction that exceeds the SPLRC's tax may be carried forward for up to five years and is not refundable. The Department's February 2026 handout states the same rates, minimum, maximum, and dates.
contact_name: Sam Komo, Captive Program Manager
types_allowed: Sponsored captive insurance companies and protected cells

fees.licensing_incorporation: Section 379.1302 requires a nonrefundable license fee of $7,500 for examining, investigating, and processing the application. The director may charge the applicant the reasonable cost of outside legal, financial, and examination services. The renewal fee is $7,500. 20 CSR 200-20.030 states a $7,500 license fee for initial admission and, for a special purpose life reinsurance captive, an additional application fee of $10,000. The Department's February 2026 handout states the ordinary license fee as $7,500 and the SPLRC application fee and license fee as $17,500. It also states an actuarial application-review fee of $4,000, or $7,500 for an SPLRC, invoiced by the actuarial firm the Department assigns. Secretary of State organization fees are not set in the captive sections.
fees.annual_fees: Annual renewal fee of $7,500 (section 379.1302 and section 379.1364). The ordinary license authorizes business until 1 April. The Department's handout states the ordinary renewal date as 1 April and the SPLRC renewal date as 1 March. The license fee and the renewal fee may be deducted from premium tax. The handout states that the actuarial review fee is paid to the assigned actuarial firm.
fees.premium_tax_rate: Direct premiums: 0.380 percent, 0.285 percent, 0.190 percent, and 0.072 percent on successive $20 million bands. Assumed reinsurance: 0.214 percent, 0.143 percent, 0.048 percent, and 0.024 percent on the same bands. An SPLRC pays the assumed-reinsurance schedule under section 379.1412. Annual minimum $7,500. Annual maximum $200,000. For a sponsored captive the minimum applies to the company as a whole, and the company remits the aggregate of the cells' tax liabilities. Return due 1 February. Tax due 1 May.

annual_filing_requirements: Before 1 March, each captive submits a report of its financial condition verified by two executive officers (section 379.1312). Reporting uses generally accepted accounting principles unless the director approves statutory accounting principles. An association captive files in the form required by section 375.041. A pure or industrial insured captive may be allowed to report on a fiscal year-end. The report is then due 60 days after fiscal year-end, and a balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows for the calendar year-end is still filed before 1 March to support the premium-tax return. 20 CSR 200-20.040 requires an annual audit by an independent certified public accountant, unless the director waives it. The audited report is due 30 June for a 31 December year-end, or within six months after an approved fiscal year-end. An SPLRC's audited report is due 31 May under that rule, and section 379.1403 requires it no later than five months after fiscal year-end. The audit includes an opinion on the adequacy of loss and loss-expense reserves by a member of the American Academy of Actuaries whom the director approves. An SPLRC, and a company providing life or annuity contracts, also includes the opinion described in section 376.380. An SPLRC files statutory-accounting financial information by 1 March. The premium-tax return is due 1 February and payment is due 1 May. The board meets at least once each year in Missouri, the principal place of business is in Missouri, a registered agent is appointed, and the captive holds at least 35 percent of its assets in Missouri or through a Missouri financial institution the director approves. Section 379.1314 requires an examination at least once every three years, which the director may enlarge to five years if the captive has a comprehensive annual audit of a scope the director accepts by independent auditors the director approves. The examination is at the captive's cost. A captive may not provide personal motor vehicle or homeowners insurance, may not write workers' compensation directly, and may not transact business as a risk retention group. It may provide excess workers' compensation and may reinsure a qualified self-insured workers' compensation plan of its parent and affiliates.

name: Montana
summary: Montana licenses captive insurers under Title 33, Chapter 28, MCA, enacted in 2001 and administered by the Captive Insurance Team of the Commissioner of Securities and Insurance. The chapter covers pure, association, industrial insured, special purpose, protected cell, branch, and captive reinsurance companies, and captive risk retention groups. Protected cells must be incorporated. A special purpose captive's capital is an amount the commissioner sets after reviewing the business plan, and a special purpose captive may use a series of members in a limited liability company. The 2025 CSI brochure states that the captive count is 279: 56 pure, 9 special purpose, 12 reinsurance, 1 association, 3 protected cell structures, 17 protected cells, 9 series LLC structures, 165 series business units, and 7 risk retention groups. The same brochure states that 41 captives were licensed in 2024, that 26 companies had been formed as of 1 June 2025, and that Montana has licensed more than 900 captives since 2001. The captive page states that Montana has nearly 300 domiciled captives, that captive insurance contributes $5 million annually to the Montana economy, and that Montana is the fifth-largest U.S. captive domicile. Unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus is at least $250,000 for a pure captive and $500,000 for an association captive, an industrial insured captive, or a captive risk retention group. A protected cell captive holds at least $500,000, which the commissioner may reduce to not less than $250,000 if the core assumes no risk, the cells' risks are homogeneous, and there are not more than 10 cells. A captive reinsurance company holds at least 50 percent of the capital required for its type. A dormant captive maintains at least $25,000. Direct premium tax is 0.4 percent on the first $20 million and 0.3 percent thereafter. Assumed-reinsurance premium tax is 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, and 0.050 percent. The annual minimum is $5,000 and the annual maximum is $100,000. The maximum does not apply to a protected cell captive or to a special purpose captive with a series of members. The application fee is $200 and the license and annual renewal fee is $300, charged as well to each series and each protected cell. The certificate is effective until 1 March. Examinations of captives other than risk retention groups are at the commissioner's discretion. A captive risk retention group is examined at least every five years. No standard licensing turnaround is published. The published contact is the Captive Insurance Team at captives@mt.gov.
legislation: Montana Captive Insurance Companies Act, Title 33, Chapter 28, Montana Code Annotated, and ARM Title 6, Chapter 6, Subchapter 68
applicable_legislation: Title 33, Chapter 28, MCA, enacted by Chapter 298, Laws of 2001, and published as the 2025 Montana Code Annotated. Capital and surplus are 33-28-104. The certificate, lines of business, in-state meeting, and fees are 33-28-102. Reports are 33-28-107. Examinations are 33-28-108. Premium tax is 33-28-201, amended by Chapter 548, Laws of 2025. Dormant captives are 33-28-401. The Commissioner cites ARM 6.6.6801 through 6.6.6821 for the annual audit and ARM 6.6.6816 for certification of loss reserves.

min_capital.Pure captive: Not less than $250,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus (33-28-104(1)(a)).
min_capital.Special purpose captive: An amount determined by the commissioner after considering the business plan, feasibility study, and pro forma documents, including the nature of the risks to be insured (33-28-104(1)(d)). The statute does not set a dollar floor.
min_capital.Protected cell captive: Not less than $500,000. If the protected cell captive assumes no risks, the risks insured by the cells are homogeneous, and there are not more than 10 cells, the commissioner may reduce the amount to not less than $250,000 (33-28-104(1)(e)). Section 33-28-101 requires every protected cell to be incorporated. The statute does not set a separate dollar floor for an individual cell.
min_capital.Branch captive: Not less than the capital and surplus required for the foreign captive's organizational form under 33-28-104(1)(a) through (1)(e). The minimum is held jointly by the commissioner and the branch in a Federal Reserve System bank the commissioner approves.
min_capital.Captive reinsurance company: Not less than 50 percent of the capital that would be required for that type of captive (33-28-104(1)(g)).
min_capital.Dormant captive: Not less than $25,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus while a certificate of dormancy is in force (33-28-401). A risk retention group cannot be dormant under that section.
min_capital.Form of capital: Cash, a cash equivalent, or an irrevocable letter of credit on the commissioner's form, issued by a Montana-chartered bank, a Federal Reserve member bank, or another state-chartered bank the commissioner approves. The commissioner may require additional capital based on the type, volume, and nature of the business (33-28-104).

tax_notes: Section 33-28-201 requires the tax by 1 March. Direct premiums, after return premiums and policyholder dividends or premium deposits returned or credited, are taxed at 0.4 percent on the first $20 million and 0.3 percent on each subsequent dollar. Assumed-reinsurance premiums are taxed at 0.225 percent on the first $20 million, 0.150 percent on the next $20 million, and 0.050 percent thereafter. Reinsurance tax does not apply to risks taxed on a direct basis, or to a qualifying assumption of loss reserves and other liabilities of another insurer under common ownership and control that is part of a plan to discontinue that insurer. If the direct and assumed taxes are under $5,000, the tax is $5,000. In the year a captive subject to the minimum is first authorized, or surrenders its certificate, the minimum is prorated by quarter. Each protected cell is considered separately in determining the aggregate tax. Each series of members of a special purpose captive is considered separately, except that the minimum tax is considered in the aggregate. The annual maximum is $100,000. That maximum does not apply to a protected cell captive or to a special purpose captive with a series of members. Two or more captives under common ownership and control, defined as 80 percent of the voting stock or, for mutuals, 80 percent of the surplus and voting power, are taxed as one captive. Only the branch business of a branch captive is taxed. A dormant captive is not liable for the section 33-28-201 tax. It pays a $1,000 annual dormancy tax by 1 March for any portion of the preceding year in which it held the certificate, and each series or protected cell is considered separate for that $1,000 tax. The certificate of dormancy expires after five consecutive years and may not be renewed. The captive page requires electronic premium-tax filing.

types_allowed: Special purpose captive insurance companies, including a series of members in a limited liability company
Protected cell captive insurance companies and incorporated protected cells
Dormant captive insurance companies holding a certificate of dormancy, other than captive risk retention groups

fees.licensing_incorporation: Section 33-28-102(4) requires a nonrefundable fee of $200 for examining, investigating, and processing the application of each captive, each individual series of members, and each protected cell. The commissioner may retain outside legal, financial, and examination services and charge the reasonable cost to the applicant. The captive page states the same $200 application fee together with a $300 license fee. Secretary of State organization fees are not set in Chapter 28.
fees.annual_fees: A fee of $300 for the year of registration and a renewal fee of $300 for each later year, payable by each captive, each individual series of members, and each protected cell (33-28-102(4)(b)). The certificate is effective until 1 March and may be renewed. A dormant captive is not otherwise liable for the section 33-28-102 annual renewal and instead pays the $1,000 dormancy tax.
fees.premium_tax_rate: Direct premiums: 0.4 percent on the first $20 million and 0.3 percent thereafter. Assumed reinsurance: 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, and 0.050 percent. Annual minimum $5,000, prorated by quarter in the year of first authorization and in the year the certificate is surrendered. Annual maximum $100,000, which does not apply to a protected cell captive or to a special purpose captive with a series of members. Due 1 March. A dormant captive pays a $1,000 dormancy tax instead of the premium tax.

annual_filing_requirements: On or before 1 April, a captive other than a risk retention group submits a report of its financial condition, verified by two executive officers. A captive risk retention group submits its report on or before 1 March and files the NAIC property-and-casualty blank with the commissioner and with the NAIC, on an annual and quarterly basis. Reporting uses generally accepted accounting principles unless the commissioner requires statutory accounting principles. A captive other than a risk retention group may be allowed to report on a fiscal year-end. The report is then due 90 days after fiscal year-end, and a report supporting the premium-tax return is still filed before 1 April for the prior calendar year. A branch captive files, by 1 April, copies of the reports required in the jurisdiction where the foreign captive is formed. Premium tax is due 1 March. The captive page states that premium tax is filed electronically, and it states that captives other than risk retention groups may file the Montana short-form annual statement by 1 April. The same page states that ARM 6.6.6801 through 6.6.6821 require an annual audit by an independent certified public accountant the commissioner approves, and that ARM 6.6.6816 requires loss and loss-expense reserves to be certified by a Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society, a member of the American Academy of Actuaries, or another person who has demonstrated competence in loss-reserve evaluation and whom the commissioner approves. The board, the board of managing members, or a reciprocal's subscribers' advisory committee meets at least once each year in Montana. The principal place of business is in Montana, and at least one director, or one manager of a limited liability company, is a Montana resident. A captive risk retention group has at least five directors. Books and records needed for a statutory examination are kept in Montana. The commissioner may examine a captive as often as the commissioner considers advisable. A captive risk retention group is examined at least every five years. The examination is at the captive's cost. A dormant captive files a financial-condition report within 90 days of each fiscal year-end and is not subject to examination under 33-28-108 while the certificate of dormancy is in force.

name: Nevada
summary: Nevada licenses captive insurers under NRS Chapter 694C, added in 1999 and administered by the Captive Section of the Nevada Division of Insurance. A captive may be a pure, association, agency, rental, or sponsored captive, an alien or branch captive, or a state-chartered risk retention group, and a sponsored captive may establish protected cells. The Division's captive homepage states that Nevada offers a series structure that lets sponsored captives create protected cells with independent corporate structures. A white paper on protected cells and the series LLC is listed on the forms page as not yet published, and Chapter 694C itself authorizes protected cells rather than using the term series LLC. The Division's 2025 Insurance Market Report states that, as of October 2024, Nevada had 147 captive insurers and 135 sponsored captive cells, and that Nevada ranked 10th as a U.S. domicile. That report does not publish a type split, a formation count, or a surrender count with those figures. A separate sentence in the same report refers to approximately 91 captives and 160 cells; that sentence is approximate and does not match the dated census, so it is not used here. Unimpaired paid-in capital and unencumbered surplus are at least $200,000 for a pure captive, $500,000 for an association captive, a sponsored captive, or a state-chartered risk retention group, $600,000 for an agency captive, and $800,000 for a rental captive. A dormant captive, a status added in 2019, maintains at least $25,000. Direct premium tax is 0.4 percent, 0.2 percent, and 0.075 percent on successive $20 million bands. Assumed-reinsurance premium tax under NRS 694C.450 is 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, and 0.025 percent on the same bands. The Division's annual-filings page prints 0.255 percent on the first reinsurance band; the statute and the application-fees page both state 0.225 percent, and this profile uses 0.225 percent. The annual minimum tax is $5,000 and the annual maximum is $175,000. For a sponsored captive the maximum applies to each protected cell and not to the sponsor as a whole. Nevada has no state income tax. The nonrefundable application fee is $500, license issuance and annual renewal are $300, and NRS 680C.110 adds a $250 initial fee and a $250 annual fee for a captive insurer. The Division states the combined application charge as $1,050 and the annual renewal as $550, due by March 1. A captive licensed after 1 July 2003 receives a one-time nonrefundable $5,000 credit against the first year in which premium tax is owed. The board meets at least once each year in Nevada. The contact page names Michael Reynolds, Management Analyst, as captive staff and does not give him a program-head title or publish a section headcount. No standard licensing turnaround is published.
legislation: Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 694C (Captive Insurers) and Nevada Administrative Code Chapter 694C
applicable_legislation: NRS Chapter 694C, added in 1999. Capital and surplus are NRS 694C.250. The certificate of dormancy was added in 2019 as NRS 694C.259 and amended in 2021. Application and license fees are NRS 694C.220 and 694C.230, plus the captive-insurer fee in NRS 680C.110. The annual report is NRS 694C.400. Examinations are NRS 694C.410. Premium tax is NRS 694C.450, amended in 2025, and branch tax is NRS 694C.455. Sponsored captives and protected cells are NRS 694C.195. Authorized insurance is NRS 694C.300, also amended in 2025. Annual-report and audit detail is also in NAC Chapter 694C.

min_capital.Pure captive: Not less than $200,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and unencumbered surplus (NRS 694C.250(1)(a)).
min_capital.Sponsored captive: Not less than $500,000 (NRS 694C.250(1)(e)). Chapter 694C does not state a separate dollar floor for an individual protected cell.
min_capital.Dormant captive: Not less than $25,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus while a certificate of dormancy is in force (NRS 694C.259(3)(a)).
min_capital.Form of capital: Cash or an irrevocable letter of credit, unless the Commissioner prescribes otherwise. A letter of credit must be issued by a Nevada-chartered bank or a Federal Reserve member bank the Commissioner approves, and it must renew automatically unless the issuer gives 90 days' notice. A Commissioner-approved surplus note may also evidence capital and surplus. The Commissioner may require additional capital based on the type, volume, and nature of the business (NRS 694C.250).

tax_notes: NRS 694C.450 imposes premium tax due not later than 1 March. Net direct premiums are taxed at two-fifths of 1 percent on the first $20 million, one-fifth of 1 percent on the next $20 million, and seventy-five thousandths of 1 percent thereafter. Assumed-reinsurance premiums are taxed at 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, and 0.025 percent on those same bands. Reinsurance tax is not levied on risks already taxed as direct premiums, and it is not levied on a qualifying assumption of loss reserves from an insurer under common ownership and control that is being discontinued. If the calculated tax is less than $5,000, the tax is $5,000. The maximum aggregate tax is $175,000. For a sponsored captive that maximum applies to each protected cell and does not apply to the sponsored captive as a whole. Two or more captives under common ownership and control, defined as 80 percent ownership, are taxed as one captive. The premium tax is in lieu of other Nevada occupation and local taxes, except the taxes in NRS Chapters 363A, 363B, and 363C and ad valorem taxes on real or personal property in Nevada used to produce income. A captive licensed after 1 July 2003 receives a nonrefundable $5,000 credit against the first year in which it owes the tax, and not more than once. A dormant captive is not liable for the tax while the certificate of dormancy is in force. Branch tax applies only to branch business. The Division's FAQ states that Nevada has no state income tax. The Division's annual-filings page prints a 0.255 percent rate on the first $20 million of reinsurance premiums. NRS 694C.450(2)(a) and the application-fees page state 0.225 percent, and the 0.225 percent rate is used here.

fees.licensing_incorporation: NRS 694C.220 requires a nonrefundable application fee of $500. NRS 694C.230 requires $300 for issuance of the license. NRS 680C.110 requires a $250 initial fee for a captive insurer. The Division's annual-filings page states that those three amounts are collected together as a $1,050 application fee. Outside legal, financial, and examination services used to review the application are paid by the applicant. The Division's application-fees page also lists an incorporation fee of $75 minimum. Secretary of State formation fees are separate from the Division's $1,050 figure.
fees.annual_fees: NRS 694C.230 requires an annual license fee of $300 on or before 1 March, plus the fees required by NRS 680C.110. NRS 680C.110 sets the captive-insurer annual fee at $250. The Division states the combined annual license renewal as $550, due by 1 March. A dormant captive continues to pay the annual fee and the NRS 680C.110 renewal fees.
fees.premium_tax_rate: Direct premiums: 0.4 percent on the first $20 million, 0.2 percent on the next $20 million, and 0.075 percent thereafter. Assumed reinsurance premiums: 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, and 0.025 percent on the same bands. Annual minimum $5,000. Annual maximum $175,000, applied per protected cell for a sponsored captive. Due 1 March. One-time $5,000 credit in the first year tax is owed, for a captive licensed after 1 July 2003.

annual_filing_requirements: By 1 March, a captive files its premium-tax return, its business plan, and the $550 annual renewal. By 30 June, a captive other than a state-chartered risk retention group files a GAAP financial-condition report, with modifications the Commissioner accepts, an audited financial statement certified by an independent certified public accountant, and an actuarial opinion. A pure captive may be allowed to file the annual report within 60 days after its parent's fiscal year-end, and it still files the premium-tax support by 1 March. A state-chartered risk retention group files on the schedule in NRS 680A.270 and files its financial statement under NRS 680A.265. A late financial report, audit, or risk-retention-group statement draws $100 a day, up to $3,000. A sponsored captive's 30 June report includes the financial experience of each protected cell. Filings are uploaded through the Division's financial-filing portal. A dormant captive does not file the NRS 694C.400 annual report, an audit, or an actuarial opinion while the certificate is in force. The certificate of dormancy is renewed after five years. Examinations are at least every three years, or every five years if the Commissioner accepts comprehensive annual audits by an appointed independent auditor. That cycle does not apply to a pure captive, which the Commissioner may examine at any reasonable time. The examination is at the captive's cost. The board meets at least once each year in Nevada, the principal place of business is in Nevada, and at least one director, or one member of a reciprocal's subscribers' advisory committee or its attorney-in-fact, is a Nevada resident.

name: New Jersey

The commissioner holds discretionary authority to increase capital requirements based on the volume and nature of insurance.

name: New Zealand
summary: New Zealand does not have specific captive-only legislation, instead governing all insurance through the IPSA 2010 act. Captives are explicitly exempt from the financial strength rating requirements that apply to traditional insurers. To obtain a license, a captive must demonstrate 'fitness for business' and the capacity to manage its specific risks.

name: North Carolina
summary: North Carolina enacted the Captive Insurance Act in 2013 (Session Law 2013-116), now Part 9 of Article 10 of Chapter 58 of the General Statutes, and regulates captives through the Department of Insurance Captive Insurance Companies Division. At year-end 2025 the Department reported 263 captive insurance companies and 746 cells and series, including conditional licenses and approvals, for more than 1,000 risk-bearing entities. Those 263 companies were 188 pure captives, 48 protected cell captives, 9 risk retention groups, and 18 special purpose captives. During 2025 the state licensed 21 captive insurers, counting new formations and redomestications, and approved approximately 80 cells and series. Statutory capital floors are $250,000 for pure, protected cell, and special purpose captives, or another amount the Commissioner sets; $500,000 for association and industrial insured captives; $1,000,000 for a risk retention group; and $250,000 in cash for a special purpose financial captive. Direct premium tax is 0.4% on the first $20 million and 0.3% above that. The ordinary minimum is $5,000 and the ordinary maximum is $100,000. The redomestication premium-tax holiday expired for taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2026.
legislation: North Carolina Captive Insurance Act (Chapter 58, Article 10, Part 9 of the General Statutes)
applicable_legislation: North Carolina General Statutes Chapter 58, Article 10, Part 9 (Captive Insurance Companies), enacted by Session Law 2013-116 and amended by Session Laws 2014-65, 2015-99, 2016-78, 2018-120, 2022-7, and 2024-29. Capital and surplus are in G.S. 58-10-370. Special purpose financial captive capital is in G.S. 58-10-575 and the application fee is in G.S. 58-10-565. Annual reports are in G.S. 58-10-405 and the annual audit is in G.S. 58-10-415. Inactive captives are in G.S. 58-10-490. The captive premium tax is G.S. 105-228.4A.

min_capital.Pure: Not less than $250,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus, or another amount determined by the Commissioner (G.S. 58-10-370(a)(1)).
min_capital.Association: Not less than $500,000 (G.S. 58-10-370(a)(2)). The Commissioner may prescribe additional capital.
min_capital.Industrial insured: Not less than $500,000 (G.S. 58-10-370(a)(3)). The Commissioner may prescribe additional capital.
min_capital.Risk retention group: Not less than $1,000,000 (G.S. 58-10-370(a)(4)). The Commissioner may prescribe additional capital.
min_capital.Protected cell: Not less than $250,000, or another amount determined by the Commissioner (G.S. 58-10-370(a)(5)).
min_capital.Special purpose: Not less than $250,000, or another amount determined by the Commissioner (G.S. 58-10-370(a)(6)).
min_capital.Special purpose financial captive: Not less than $250,000 of initial capital, all in cash. The Commissioner may require additional capital after reviewing the plan of operation, feasibility study, pro formas, and the risks insured or reinsured (G.S. 58-10-575).
min_capital.Branch captive: A branch captive is a pure captive for its North Carolina operations unless the Commissioner permits otherwise (G.S. 58-10-340). As security for branch liabilities it must hold an amount equal to the pure-captive minimum plus reserves on branch business, with a credit the Commissioner may allow for security already posted (G.S. 58-10-535).
min_capital.Inactive captive: Unimpaired capital and surplus in an amount determined by the Commissioner (G.S. 58-10-490). A risk retention group cannot be declared inactive.
min_capital.Form of capital: Cash, securities approved by the Commissioner, a clean irrevocable letter of credit from a bank the Commissioner approves, or another approved form (G.S. 58-10-370(c)). Special purpose financial captive minimum initial capital must be cash.

tax_notes: G.S. 105-228.4A taxes a North Carolina captive, and taxes only the branch business of a branch captive. A foreign captive is not subject to this tax. Direct premiums, after return premiums, are taxed at 0.4% up to $20 million and 0.3% above $20 million. Assumed reinsurance premiums are taxed at 0.225% up to $20 million, 0.150% from $20 million to $40 million, 0.050% from $40 million to $60 million, and 0.025% above $60 million. Assumed-reinsurance tax does not apply to risks already taxed as direct premiums, or to a qualifying assumption of reserves between commonly controlled insurers that is part of a plan to discontinue one insurer. For any captive other than the multi-cell case below, the tax is at least $5,000 and at most $100,000. A protected cell captive with more than 10 cells, or a special purpose captive with a cell or series structure of more than 10 cells or series, pays at least $10,000 and at most the lesser of $100,000 plus $5,000 for each cell or series over 10, and $200,000. Two or more captives under common ownership and control are taxed as one captive, except a protected cell captive and a special purpose captive with a cell or series structure. The premium-tax report and payment are due by March 15. Captives subject to this tax are not subject to the franchise tax, to income tax except as G.S. 105-130.5A provides, to local privilege or local gross-premium taxes, or to the insurance regulatory charge. The redomestication holiday in G.S. 105-228.4A(g) expired for taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2026. An inactive captive is not liable for tax under Article 8B of Chapter 105 for any full year it is inactive (G.S. 58-10-490).

Ordinary minimum $5,000 and ordinary maximum $100,000. A protected cell captive with more than 10 cells, or a special purpose captive with more than 10 cells or series, has a $10,000 minimum and a maximum of the lesser of $100,000 plus $5,000 per cell or series over 10, and $200,000. The redomestication tax holiday expired for taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2026.

annual_filing_requirements: Each captive submits a report of its financial condition as of the preceding December 31, verified by two executive officers, before March 15. Reporting is on generally accepted accounting principles unless the Commissioner requires or accepts another basis (G.S. 58-10-405). A pure, special purpose, or industrial insured captive may be allowed to file 75 days after its fiscal year-end. The annual audit and statement of actuarial opinion for captives other than risk retention groups are due by June 30, or within 180 days after an approved fiscal year-end (G.S. 58-10-415). Risk retention groups file under Parts 6 and 7 of Article 10 instead of that audit section. The premium-tax report and payment are due by March 15 (G.S. 105-228.4A). The Department's filing page for 2026 also lists Form C-202, the direct economic impact supplement, and Form C-207 for inactive captives. Filings are submitted electronically through the Department's online system or to the Captive Insurance Administrator. The Commissioner may waive the annual report if the annual audit is filed, and may grant a hardship exemption from the audit, but may not waive both at the same time. A request to skip the annual report is due at least 30 days before the report due date.

name: Oklahoma
summary: Oklahoma licenses captive insurers under the Oklahoma Captive Insurance Company Act, Title 36, sections 6470.1 through 6470.35, first enacted as Chapter 334, Oklahoma Session Laws 2004, and administered by the Captive Insurance Division of the Oklahoma Insurance Department. A pure captive holds at least $250,000, of which $150,000 is paid in before the license is issued and the remaining $100,000 is paid in by the first anniversary. An association captive incorporated as a stock insurer holds at least $750,000, an industrial insured captive incorporated as a stock insurer at least $500,000, a sponsored captive at least $500,000, and a risk retention group at least $1,000,000. A special purpose or branch captive holds at least $250,000 or another amount the commissioner sets. A series captive's capital is an amount the commissioner specifies. Direct premium tax is 0.2 percent and assumed-reinsurance premium tax is 0.1 percent, due 1 March. The ordinary minimum is $5,000 and the maximum is $100,000. A series captive's annual minimum is $3,500. The nonrefundable application fee is $200, or $300 for a special purpose captive, and the license and renewal fee is $300. The Division states that it will process a completed license application within 30 to 45 business days. The commissioner may issue a provisional license. The Department's 2025 annual report states that 2024 ended with 64 captive insurers, after a net gain of five. The 19 February 2026 release states that in 2025 the Department approved all 14 applications it received, four captives dissolved, and the net gain was 10, surpassing the 2017 high of 73. That release does not state the 31 December 2025 headcount. There is no in-state manager, in-state board member, or in-state annual board-meeting requirement. Applications and questions go to oidcaptive@oid.ok.gov. Steve Kinion is Director of the Captive Insurance Division. No current staff count is published.
legislation: Oklahoma Captive Insurance Company Act, Title 36, Oklahoma Statutes, sections 6470.1 through 6470.35, and Oklahoma Administrative Code 365:25-15-1 through 365:25-15-23
applicable_legislation: The Oklahoma Captive Insurance Company Act originated as Chapter 334, Oklahoma Session Laws 2004. Enrolled House Bill 2905 (2006) cites that chapter as the source of the captive sections. Capital and surplus are section 6470.6, as restated by enrolled Senate Bill 1035 (2021). The license, fees, and provisional license are section 6470.3, as restated by enrolled Senate Bill 1242, effective 1 November 2022. Reports are section 6470.11, as restated by Senate Bill 1035. Examinations are section 6470.13, as amended by enrolled House Bill 1108 (2013). Premium tax is section 6470.19, as restated by Senate Bill 1035. Dormancy is section 6470.35, as amended by enrolled Senate Bill 1240, effective 1 November 2022. The Department posts OAC 365:25-15 as its captive rules.

min_capital.Pure captive: Not less than $250,000 of unimpaired aggregate paid-in capital and surplus. $150,000 must be paid in before the license is issued, and an additional $100,000 must be paid in on or before the first anniversary (36 O.S. section 6470.6(A)(1), Senate Bill 1035).
min_capital.Association captive: Not less than $750,000 for an association captive incorporated as a stock insurer (section 6470.6(A)(2)).
min_capital.Industrial insured captive: Not less than $500,000 for an industrial insured captive incorporated as a stock insurer (section 6470.6(A)(3)).
min_capital.Sponsored captive: Not less than $500,000 (section 6470.6(A)(4)). The statute does not set a separate dollar floor for an individual protected cell.
min_capital.Risk retention group: Not less than $1,000,000 for a captive doing business as a risk retention group (section 6470.6(A)(5)).
min_capital.Special purpose or branch captive: Not less than $250,000, or an amount determined by the commissioner after considering the business plan, feasibility study, and pro formas, including the nature of the risks to be insured (section 6470.6(A)(6)). The Department's types page states the same standard.
min_capital.Series captive: An amount specified by the commissioner (section 6470.6(A)(7)). The statute does not set a dollar floor. The Department's types page states the same standard.
min_capital.Dormant captive: Not less than $25,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus while a certificate of dormancy is in force (section 6470.35, Senate Bill 1240).
min_capital.Form of capital: Cash, a cash equivalent, or an irrevocable letter of credit issued by an Oklahoma-chartered bank or a Federal Reserve member bank, and approved by the commissioner. The commissioner may prescribe additional capital based on the type, volume, and nature of the business. For a branch captive, the commissioner may require a U.S. trust, funded by an irrevocable letter of credit or other acceptable asset, of not less than the required capital and surplus plus the reserves on branch policies and reinsurance contracts.

tax_notes: Section 6470.19, as restated by Senate Bill 1035, taxes each captive other than a sponsored captive, and each protected cell of a sponsored captive, at 0.2 percent of direct premiums after return premiums and policyholder dividends or premium deposits returned or credited. Annuity considerations are not taxed. Assumed-reinsurance premium is taxed at 0.1 percent. Reinsurance tax does not apply to risks taxed on a direct basis, or to a qualifying assumption of loss reserves and other liabilities of another insurer under common ownership and control that is part of a plan to discontinue that insurer. A sponsored captive pays, in the aggregate, the minimum tax. If the calculated tax is under $5,000, the tax is $5,000. In the year a captive is first licensed, or a protected cell is first approved, that minimum is prorated by quarter: $5,000, $3,750, $2,500, or $1,250. A series captive pays an annual minimum aggregate tax of $3,500. The tax paid by more than one series formed in one limited liability company or statutory trust is not restricted by the annual maximum. If the calculated tax exceeds $100,000, the tax is $100,000, subject to the common-ownership and employment provisions. Captives under common ownership and control, defined as 80 percent of the voting stock or other voting interests, are taxed as one captive, and protected cells under that ownership are taxed as one cell. A captive that employed 25 or more qualified individuals in Oklahoma throughout the tax year, and that would otherwise owe more than $50,000, pays $50,000. A qualified individual is employed in Oklahoma at least 35 hours a week by the captive or by a wholly owned subsidiary that provides management, operating, investment, or related services only to that captive. The tax is in lieu of other Oklahoma occupation taxes, except ad valorem taxes on real and personal property used to produce income. The return is due 1 March. The Department requires the filing through OPTins. A dormant captive is not liable for the section 6470 tax during the initial five-year dormancy (section 6470.35).

types_allowed: Sponsored captive insurance companies and protected cells, including entity-protected cells

fees.licensing_incorporation: Section 6470.3, as restated by Senate Bill 1242, requires a nonrefundable application fee of $200 to review whether the application is complete. A special purpose captive pays a nonrefundable fee of $300. The commissioner may also charge the reasonable cost of outside legal, financial, and examination services. The license fee for the year of registration is $300. The formation page states that the filing includes a $200 review fee and a $300 license fee. A provisional license requires the same fees. Organization fees payable to the Oklahoma Secretary of State are not set in the Captive Insurance Company Act.
fees.annual_fees: Annual license renewal fee of $300 (section 6470.3). The license authorizes business until the succeeding 1 March, when it may be renewed. A dormant captive pays a nonrefundable annual fee of $500 (section 6470.35) rather than the premium tax during the initial five-year dormancy. The certificate of dormancy is renewed every five years and is forfeited if it is not renewed.
fees.premium_tax_rate: Direct premiums: 0.2 percent. Assumed reinsurance premiums: 0.1 percent. Ordinary minimum $5,000, prorated by quarter in the year of first licensure or first cell approval. Series-captive minimum $3,500. Annual maximum $100,000. A captive employing 25 or more qualified Oklahoma individuals pays $50,000 if it would otherwise owe more. Due 1 March through OPTins. A dormant captive owes no section 6470 tax during the initial five years of dormancy.

annual_filing_requirements: Before 1 March, a captive submits a report of its financial condition verified by two executive officers (section 6470.11). Reporting uses generally accepted accounting principles unless the commissioner approves statutory accounting principles or international accounting standards. A pure captive may be allowed to file on its parent's fiscal year. The statute then requires the annual report 60 days after fiscal year-end, and pages 1 through 7 of the Captive Annual Statement for the calendar year-end before 1 March to support the premium-tax return. OAC 365:25-15-3, in the rules PDF the Department posts, states that an approved pure-captive fiscal-year report is filed no later than 180 days after fiscal year-end. The audited financial report is due 30 June for a 31 December year-end. The same rule says a pure captive approved to report on a fiscal year files that report no later than 180 days after fiscal year-end. The commissioner may exempt a company with direct written and assumed premiums of $2,000,000 or less in the preceding year from the annual audit, and may exempt a company at that premium level from the annual actuarial opinion. The actuarial opinion certifies life, health, or annuity reserves, or loss and loss-expense reserves, and is given by a member of the American Academy of Actuaries or the Casualty Actuarial Society who meets the U.S. qualification standards, or by another person who has demonstrated competence in loss-reserve evaluation. A risk retention group files the report required by Title 36, section 311. Premium tax is filed through OPTins and is due 1 March. The Department states there is no in-state manager, in-state board member, or in-state annual board-meeting requirement. A captive maintains a place of business in Oklahoma designated as its registered office and appoints a resident registered agent. Section 6470.13, as amended by House Bill 1108, requires an examination at least once in five years, which the commissioner may enlarge to seven years if the captive is subject to a comprehensive annual audit of a scope the commissioner accepts, by independent auditors the commissioner approves. A dormant captive files a financial-condition report by 1 March. The rules PDF the Department still links, last amended effective 1 November 2021, describes an earlier dormancy tax. The profile follows section 6470.35 as amended in 2022.

name: Singapore
summary: After licensing its first captive in 1983, Singapore has grown into the largest Asia Pacific captive domicile and a major reinsurance center. Capital adequacy is set strictly such that equity and retained earnings must exceed the sum of SGD 400,000 and calculated insurance fund components.

name: South Carolina
summary: South Carolina has licensed captive insurers since the enabling law of 2000, now Title 38, Chapter 90 of the Code of Laws, and supervises them through the Department of Insurance Captive Insurance Division. The South Carolina Department of Insurance confirmed 245 active captive insurance companies as of November 2026 (regulator correspondence), and the Division reported 15 new licenses in 2025. A pure captive must hold at least $250,000. An industrial insured captive or a risk retention group must hold at least $500,000, and an association captive at least $750,000. A special purpose financial captive's minimum initial capital is $250,000 in cash. Sponsored captives, and special purpose captives that are not risk retention groups, have capital set by the director. Direct premium tax is 0.4% on the first $20 million and 0.3% after that. Assumed-reinsurance tax steps from 0.225% down to 0.025%. The combined tax has a $5,000 minimum, prorated in the year a captive is first licensed, and a $100,000 maximum. After a completed application, the Division expects licensing to take 30 to 45 days, with additional time possible for a special purpose financial captive.
legislation: South Carolina Code of Laws, Title 38, Chapter 90 (Captive Insurance Companies)
applicable_legislation: South Carolina Code of Laws Title 38, Chapter 90, originating in 2000 Act No. 331 and including 2018 Act No. 251 and 2025 Act Nos. 42 and 62. Capitalization is §38-90-40. Licensing and the ordinary fee are §38-90-20. Annual reports are §38-90-70. Premium tax is §38-90-140. Special purpose financial captives are Article 3 of the chapter, including capitalization in §38-90-460, fees in §38-90-440, and tax in §38-90-580.

min_capital.Pure: Not less than $250,000 of free and unimpaired paid-in capital, surplus, unrestricted net assets of a nonprofit, or a combination (S.C. Code §38-90-40(A)(1)(a)).
min_capital.Association: Not less than $750,000 for an association captive incorporated as a stock insurer or mutual insurer, or organized as a limited liability company (§38-90-40(A)(1)(b)).
min_capital.Sponsored: An amount determined by the director after considering the business plan, feasibility study, and pro formas, including the nature, scale, and complexity of the risks (§38-90-40(A)(1)(d)). The Division's types page states the same case-by-case standard.
min_capital.Special purpose: For a special purpose captive that is not a risk retention group, an amount determined by the director on the same business-plan basis as a sponsored captive (§38-90-40(A)(1)(e)).
min_capital.Special purpose financial captive: Not less than $250,000. All of the minimum initial capitalization must be cash. The director may require additional capital (S.C. Code §38-90-460).
min_capital.Branch captive: Section 38-90-40(C) requires a United States trust, funded by an irrevocable letter of credit or other acceptable asset, of not less than the reserves on policies and reinsurance written through the branch, with a credit the director may allow for security already posted with a reinsurer or fronting company. The Division's types page separately lists a $250,000 statutory minimum for a branch captive under §38-90-40.
min_capital.Additional capital: The director may prescribe additional capital and surplus based on the type, volume, and nature of business to be transacted (§38-90-40(A)(2)). Required capital is held as cash, approved securities, a clean irrevocable letter of credit, or another form the director approves.

tax_notes: Under S.C. Code §38-90-140, tax is paid to the Department by March 1. Direct premiums, after return premiums, are taxed at 0.4% on the first $20 million and 0.3% on each dollar after that. Assumed reinsurance premiums are taxed at 0.225% on the first $20 million, 0.150% on the next $20 million, 0.050% on the next $20 million, and 0.025% after that. Reinsurance tax does not apply to risks already taxed on a direct basis, or to a qualifying assumption of reserves under common ownership and control that is part of a plan to discontinue the cedent's related operations. If the direct and assumed taxes together are under $5,000, the captive pays a $5,000 minimum. In the calendar year of first licensure that minimum is prorated by quarter: $5,000, $3,750, $2,500, or $1,250. If the calculated taxes exceed $100,000, the captive pays a $100,000 maximum. Captives under common ownership and control are taxed as separate companies. For a branch captive the tax applies only to branch business. For a sponsored captive, the sponsored captive and its incorporated and unincorporated protected cells are taxed on a consolidated basis as one captive. This tax is in lieu of other occupation taxes, except ad valorem taxes on real and personal property used in producing income. A special purpose financial captive is taxed under §38-90-580 at the same direct and assumed rates, with its own $5,000 minimum and $100,000 maximum, and each of its protected cells is taxed as a separate special purpose financial captive. The Division's fee schedule publishes the same $5,000 minimum and $100,000 maximum.

types_allowed: Sponsored captive insurance companies, with incorporated or unincorporated protected cells

fees.licensing_incorporation: For a captive other than a special purpose financial captive, S.C. Code §38-90-20 sets a nonrefundable $200 application-processing fee and a $300 license fee for the year of registration. The director may also charge the reasonable cost of outside legal, financial, and examination services. The Division's published schedule lists a $4,000 review fee for those captives and a $0 processing fee beside the $200 application fee. For a special purpose financial captive, §38-90-440 sets a $200 processing fee, a minimum $12,000 fee when internal resources examine the application ($6,000 on filing and the remainder on licensure) or the cost of outside services, and a $300 initial license fee. The Division schedule lists that application fee as $12,000.
fees.annual_fees: Annual renewal license fee of $500 for captives and for special purpose financial captives (§§38-90-20 and 38-90-440). A special purpose financial captive also pays an annual review fee of $2,400, or the actual cost if the director determines that cost is higher.
fees.premium_tax_rate: Direct premiums: 0.4% on the first $20 million and 0.3% thereafter. Assumed reinsurance premiums: 0.225% on the first $20 million, 0.150% on the next $20 million, 0.050% on the next $20 million, and 0.025% thereafter. Combined minimum $5,000, prorated by quarter in the year of first licensure, and combined maximum $100,000. A special purpose financial captive is taxed at the same rates under §38-90-580, and each of its protected cells is taxed separately. Due March 1.

annual_filing_requirements: A risk retention group submits its annual report by March 1. Every other captive submits its annual report by July 1. The report is verified by two executive officers and uses generally accepted accounting principles unless the director approves statutory accounting principles (S.C. Code §38-90-70). A non-risk-retention captive with a fiscal year-end other than December 31 files its income statement and premium schedule before March 1 and the full annual report within 180 days after fiscal year-end. Premium tax is due March 1 (§38-90-140). Beginning the year after licensure, the board, the managing board of a limited liability company, or the subscribers' advisory committee of a reciprocal must meet at least annually with a quorum physically present in South Carolina, including at least two members physically present in the state (§38-90-20). The Division's filing calendar also sets June 30 for the non-risk-retention actuarial opinion and audited financial statements, and it sets quarterly statements and NAIC-style filings for risk retention groups and special purpose financial captives.

name: Tennessee
summary: Tennessee regulates captives through the Department of Commerce and Insurance Captive Insurance Section under the Revised Tennessee Captive Insurance Act, Tennessee Code Title 56, Chapter 13. The department states that captive legislation was first enacted in 1978 and was thoroughly revised in 2011. The Act covers pure, association, industrial insured, agency, risk retention group, protected cell, incorporated cell, branch, and special purpose financial captives. An incorporated protected cell may be an individual series of a limited liability company, and a series cell formed after 1 July 2015 uses a series-cell name. Unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus is at least $250,000 for a pure or agency captive, $500,000 for an association or industrial insured captive, $1,000,000 for a risk retention group, and $100,000 for a protected cell captive. A special purpose financial captive starts with at least $250,000 in cash. A dormant captive holding a letter of dormancy maintains $25,000 and is not liable for the minimum premium tax. Direct premium tax is 0.4 percent on the first $20 million and 0.3 percent after that. Assumed-reinsurance tax is 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, 0.050 percent, and 0.025 percent on successive $20 million bands. The ordinary minimum is $5,000 and the ordinary maximum is $100,000. A protected cell captive with more than 10 cells has a $10,000 minimum and a maximum of $100,000 plus $5,000 for each cell over 10. An alien company redomesticating to Tennessee may elect to forgo premium tax in either its first or its second year, but not both, and a clawback applies if it leaves within five years. The Captive Statistics page lists 194 captive insurance companies: 111 pure, 79 protected cell companies, and 4 association. The newest license date on that list is 1 October 2026. The page does not state a total, a cell count, or whether every listed company is active. On 17 March 2026 the department reported five new captives and 50 new cells licensed in 2025, and 184 captives and 703 cells at that date. The Spring 2026 newsletter reported 184 captives and 705 cells. A complete application is processed in approximately 30 days.
legislation: Revised Tennessee Captive Insurance Act, Tennessee Code Annotated Title 56, Chapter 13
applicable_legislation: Tennessee Code Annotated Title 56, Chapter 13, the Revised Tennessee Captive Insurance Act. The Captive Insurance Section states that captive legislation was first enacted in 1978 and thoroughly revised by the General Assembly in 2011 (2011 Public Chapter 468). Part 1 is general provisions, including capital in section 56-13-105, annual reports in section 56-13-108, examinations in section 56-13-109, premium tax in section 56-13-114, redomestication in section 56-13-123, and dormancy in section 56-13-124. Part 2 is protected cell captive insurance companies, including series cells in section 56-13-204. Part 3 is branch captive insurance companies. Part 4 is special purpose financial captives, including minimum capitalization in section 56-13-406. Section histories through the 2025 code include 2024 Public Chapter 643.

min_capital.Pure: Not less than $250,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus (Tenn. Code Ann. section 56-13-105(a)(1)).
min_capital.Agency: Not less than $250,000 (section 56-13-105(a)(6)). An agency captive is owned by an insurance agency or brokerage and only reinsures risks of policies placed by or through that agency or brokerage.
min_capital.Protected cell: Not less than $100,000 for the protected cell captive insurance company (section 56-13-105(a)(5)). A separate statutory dollar floor for each protected cell was not stated in section 56-13-105.
min_capital.Special purpose financial captive: Initial minimum capitalization of not less than $250,000, all of it in cash (section 56-13-406(a)). The commissioner may require additional capitalization after reviewing the plan of operation, feasibility study, pro formas, and the risks.
min_capital.Dormant: A dormant captive that has been issued a letter of dormancy maintains unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus of not less than $25,000 (section 56-13-124(c)(1)).
min_capital.Additional capital and form: The commissioner may prescribe additional capital and surplus based on the type, volume, and nature of the business (section 56-13-105(b)). Capital required by subsection (a) must be cash, a cash equivalent, marketable securities meeting the statute's rating limits, or an irrevocable letter of credit from a bank the commissioner approves. The department's licensing page requires the minimum to be provided on its irrevocable letter of credit or securities account control agreement, and it does not accept changes to those forms.

tax_notes: Under Tenn. Code Ann. section 56-13-114, each captive pays the department by 15 March. Direct premiums, after return premiums, are taxed at 0.4 percent on the first $20 million and 0.3 percent on each dollar after that. Annuity considerations are not taxed. Assumed reinsurance premium is taxed at 0.225 percent on the first $20 million, 0.150 percent on the next $20 million, 0.050 percent on the next $20 million, and 0.025 percent after that. No reinsurance tax applies to risks taxed on a direct basis, or to a qualifying assumption of reserves and liabilities of an insurer under common ownership and control that the commissioner verifies is part of a plan to discontinue that insurer's operations. Except for a protected cell captive with more than 10 cells, the annual minimum aggregate tax is $5,000 and the annual maximum aggregate tax is $100,000. For a protected cell captive with more than 10 cells, the minimum is $10,000 and the maximum is $100,000 plus $5,000 multiplied by the number of cells over 10. A dormant captive with a letter of dormancy is not liable for the minimum. The section states that this tax is all the tax collectible under Tennessee law from the captive and from an insured on payments to the captive, except ad valorem taxes on real and personal property used in the production of income. A company redomesticating under section 56-13-123 is taxed only on premiums paid after redomestication. One that redomesticates after 1 July pays half the minimum tax in its first year. An alien company may elect to forgo premium tax in either its first or its second year after redomestication, but not both. If it then surrenders its license or redomesticates away within five years, it immediately pays the foregone tax plus 10 percent per year from the original due date.

A dormant captive with a letter of dormancy is not liable for the minimum. Due 15 March.

annual_filing_requirements: Before 15 March, each captive submits a report of its financial condition, verified by the oath of two executive officers, on the Captive Annual Statement Form. A risk retention group submits that report before 1 March. Reporting uses generally accepted accounting principles unless the commissioner requires, approves, or accepts statutory accounting principles or another comprehensive basis (Tenn. Code Ann. section 56-13-108). A captive other than a risk retention group may be allowed to file 75 days after its fiscal year-end, and a pure or industrial insured captive on a fiscal year still files the premium-tax support before 15 March unless the commissioner approves another tax date. The department requires loss and loss-expense reserves to be certified by a Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society, a member in good standing of the American Academy of Actuaries, or another person who has demonstrated competence in loss-reserve evaluation and whom the commissioner has approved. Captives in good standing that have an annual audit by an approved CPA are placed on a five-year examination cycle. Captives that do not have an annual audit are placed on a maximum three-year examination cycle. A dormant captive with a letter of dormancy still files the section 56-13-108 report before 15 March. Filings can be submitted through the department's CORE system.
